prediction:
THOUGHT: Newborn with failure to pass meconium and progressive abdominal distension since birth suggests a neonatal distal intestinal obstruction. Bilious vomiting indicates obstruction distal to the ampulla of Vater. Abdominal X-ray shows dilated bowel loops with no rectal gas, localizing the obstruction to the distal colon/rectum. Definitive diagnostic test is rectal biopsy; histopathology demonstrates absence of ganglion cells in the submucosal (Meissner) and myenteric (Auerbach) plexuses, which is the pathognomonic finding for congenital aganglionosis. These findings together confirm the diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS: Hirschsprung disease (congenital aganglionic megacolon)
